1# Copyright 2026 FlagOS Contributors 

2# 

3# Kunlunxin (XPU) override of igammac (aten::special_gammaincc, out-of-place). 

4# 

5# Root causes of the generic `flag_gems/ops/igammac.py` on XPU: 

6# 1. `_build_d_coeffs` builds the DLMF 8.12.4 coefficient tensor with 

7# `torch.tensor(list, dtype=..., device=flag_gems.device)`. Inside 

8# `use_gems()`/`enable()` the Kunlunxin `to_copy` override refuses 

9# CPU->XPU copies -> `NotImplementedError` before any kernel runs. 

10# 2. `tl_extra_shim.lgamma` resolves to `undefined symbol: __nv_lgammaf` at 

11# xpu3 link time (same root cause as lgamma / special_gammainc / 

12# special_gammaln / igammac_ overrides). 

13# 3. `tl_extra_shim.log1p` resolves to `undefined symbol: __nv_log1pf` at 

14# link time; no `tl.log1p` exists in the XPU Triton dialect. 

15# 4. `@triton.autotune` with 10 configs re-compiles per shape on XPU and 

16# inflates IR (harness lesson 2.1); replaced with a single BLOCK config. 

17# 

18# Fix: dedicated XPU kernel identical in math to the generic one (power 

19# series for x < a+1, continued fraction for x >= a+1, DLMF 8.12.4 

20# asymptotic expansion for large a with x ~ a, plus inf/nan/domain 

21# handling), with: 

22# - inline Lanczos g=7 log-gamma for a > 0 (`_lgamma_pos`, same helper as 

23# lgamma / special_gammainc / mvlgamma_ overrides), 

24# - fixed BLOCK=512, no autotune; fp32 only (XPU has no fp64). 

25# 

26# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

27# 2026-08-30 (XPU2) performance rewrite. The kernel is pure ALU (the memory 

28# floor for [4096, 4096] fp32 is ~0.13 ms, the kernel measured 228 ms), so 

29# every per-lane instruction inside the two runtime loops costs ~0.06 ms of 

30# wall time. Four changes, all validated against a CPU fp64 oracle at a 

31# tighter max error than the previous code (4.7e-6 -> see 

32# harness/solution/performance/igammac_xpu2_20260830.md): 

33# a) The continued fraction is evaluated *bottom-up* (backward recurrence 

34# on the N-term convergent) instead of forward modified-Lentz. Lentz 

35# needs two divisions, two `tl.abs`, two comparisons and two `tl.where` 

36# re-normalisation guards per step (~20 ops); the backward recurrence 

37# needs one division and four additions (~6 ops) and needs no guard at 

38# all because a fixed term count makes the "did it converge yet" test 

39# unnecessary. `tl.where` costs ~2x an fma on this backend, so the two 

40# guards alone were ~40% of the loop. 

41# b) Loop trip counts cut using the fp32 error floor instead of a 

42# worst-case guess: 50 -> 24 series terms and 50 -> 18 CF terms. Both 

43# plateau well before that (series 22, CF 14) on a 400k-point grid. 

44# c) `_log1p_minus_s`'s 29-iteration runtime Taylor loop (with a division 

45# and an int->float conversion per step) is replaced by a 10-term 

46# Horner polynomial in the *clamped* relative offset, so the asymptotic 

47# eta is a straight-line fma chain. 

48# d) The DLMF coefficient table no longer lives in device memory: the 

49# kernel used to issue 64 scalar `tl.load`s from `d_ptr` per element. 

50# Only c_0..c_3 matter for fp32 once a > 10, so the needed 17 

51# coefficients are inlined as literals (Triton cannot reference 

52# module-level constants at all - `NameError: Cannot access global 

53# variable` - so they are written out longhand) and the `d_ptr` 

54# argument is gone. 

55# In addition the asymptotic activation window is widened from 

56# `a > 20 & |sigma| < 0.3` to `a > 10 & |sigma| < 0.4`. That is not a 

57# speed change (all three branches are evaluated for every lane and merged 

58# with a mask-and-sum) but it moves the hardest series/CF inputs onto the 

59# cheap, more accurate expansion, which is what allows (b). 

60import logging 

61 

62import torch 

63import triton 

64import triton.language as tl 

65 

66import flag_gems 

67 

68logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

71@triton.jit 

72def _lgamma_pos(z): 

73 # Lanczos approximation of log-gamma for z > 0 (g=7, n=9 coefficients). 

74 # XPU Triton has no `lgamma` intrinsic (undefined symbol at link time), 

75 # so it is evaluated inline in fp32. gammaincc feeds a > 0 into 

76 # _lgamma_pos (the reflection branch is unnecessary since out-of-domain 

77 # a <= 0 produces NaN regardless). 

78 g = 7.0 

79 x = 0.99999999999980993 

80 x = x + 676.5203681218851 / (z + 0.0) 

81 x = x + (-1259.1392167224028) / (z + 1.0) 

82 x = x + 771.32342877765313 / (z + 2.0) 

83 x = x + (-176.61502916214059) / (z + 3.0) 

84 x = x + 12.507343278686905 / (z + 4.0) 

85 x = x + (-0.13857109526572012) / (z + 5.0) 

86 x = x + 9.9843695780195716e-6 / (z + 6.0) 

87 x = x + 1.5056327351493116e-7 / (z + 7.0) 

88 t = (z - 1.0) + g + 0.5 

89 half_log_2pi = 0.9189385332046727 

90 return half_log_2pi + ((z - 1.0) + 0.5) * tl.log(t) - t + tl.log(x)

93@triton.jit 

94def _eta_sq(sigma): 

95 # -2 * (log(1 + s) - s) = s^2 * sum_{k>=0} 2 (-1)^k / (k+2) * s^k. 

96 # 

97 # Evaluated as a Horner chain on `s` clamped to [-0.4, 0.4]: the caller 

98 # only consumes the result where |sigma| < 0.4, and clamping keeps the 

99 # unselected lanes finite (an unclamped s^9 overflows for the large-|s| 

100 # lanes and the resulting NaN, while masked out, is free to avoid). 

101 # 10 terms leave < 2e-9 relative remainder at |s| = 0.4, i.e. below the 

102 # fp32 rounding of the s^2 prefactor. 

103 # 

104 # This replaces `tl_extra_shim.log1p` (undefined symbol: __nv_log1pf on 

105 # XPU) *and* the previous 29-iteration runtime Taylor loop: no division, 

106 # no int->float conversion, no loop. 

107 s = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(sigma, -0.4), 0.4) 

108 p = -0.18181818181818182 

109 p = p * s + 0.2 

110 p = p * s + (-0.2222222222222222) 

111 p = p * s + 0.25 

112 p = p * s + (-0.2857142857142857) 

113 p = p * s + 0.3333333333333333 

114 p = p * s + (-0.4) 

115 p = p * s + 0.5 

116 p = p * s + (-0.6666666666666666) 

117 p = p * s + 1.0 

118 return tl.maximum((s * s) * p, 0.0)

121@triton.jit 

122def igammac_kernel_xpu( 

123 a_ptr, 

124 x_ptr, 

125 out_ptr, 

126 n_elements, 

127 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

128 N_SER: tl.constexpr, 

129 N_CF: tl.constexpr, 

130): 

131 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

132 offsets = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

133 mask = offsets < n_elements 

134 # other=1.0 / other=0.0: masked lanes never feed valid results (their 

135 # stores are masked out as well). 

136 a = tl.load(a_ptr + offsets, mask=mask, other=1.0) 

137 x = tl.load(x_ptr + offsets, mask=mask, other=0.0) 

138 

139 a_f = a.to(tl.float32) 

140 x_f = x.to(tl.float32) 

141 

142 # Detect inf and NaN (same edge semantics as the generic kernel). 

143 is_nan_x = x_f != x_f 

144 is_nan_a = a_f != a_f 

145 is_inf_or_nan_x = (x_f * 0.0) != 0.0 

146 is_inf_or_nan_a = (a_f * 0.0) != 0.0 

147 is_inf_x = is_inf_or_nan_x & ~is_nan_x 

148 is_inf_a = is_inf_or_nan_a & ~is_nan_a 

149 is_finite = ~is_inf_or_nan_x & ~is_inf_or_nan_a 

150 in_domain = (a_f > 0.0) & (x_f >= 0.0) & is_finite 

151 

152 log_gamma_a = _lgamma_pos(a_f) 

153 log_x_term = a_f * tl.log(x_f) - x_f - log_gamma_a 

154 

155 # Path 1: power series for P(a, x) = e^{-x} x^a sum_n x^n / Gamma(a+n+1), 

156 # then Q = 1 - P. Converges for x < a + 1. The denominator a + i is 

157 # carried incrementally (`ai`) so the loop body holds no int->float 

158 # conversion; 24 terms are past the fp32 error floor for every 

159 # (a, x) that reaches this branch (worst case a ~ 10, x ~ a + 1). 

160 term = 1.0 / a_f 

161 series_sum = term 

162 ai = a_f 

163 for _s in range(1, N_SER): 

164 ai = ai + 1.0 

165 term = term * (x_f / ai) 

166 series_sum = series_sum + term 

167 q_series = 1.0 - tl.exp(log_x_term) * series_sum 

168 

169 # Path 2: the Legendre continued fraction for Q(a, x) directly, 

170 # Q = e^{a log x - x - log Gamma(a)} / w, 

171 # w = b0 + a1/(b1 + a2/(b2 + ...)), a_n = n (a - n), b_n = x+2n+1-a. 

172 # Evaluated *backwards* from the N_CF-th convergent (w <- b_N, then 

173 # w <- b_{n-1} + a_n / w for n = N..1). Compared with forward modified 

174 # Lentz this drops one division, two `tl.abs`, two comparisons and the 

175 # two `tl.where` re-normalisation guards per step: the guards only exist 

176 # to keep a *convergence-tested* forward recurrence from dividing by 

177 # zero, and with a fixed term count there is nothing to test. 

178 # Both coefficient sequences are carried incrementally: 

179 # b_{n-1} = b_n - 2 and a_{n-1} = a_n + (b_{n-1} - x). 

180 w = x_f + (2.0 * N_CF + 1.0) - a_f 

181 b_prev = x_f + (2.0 * N_CF - 1.0) - a_f 

182 an = (a_f - (1.0 * N_CF)) * (1.0 * N_CF) 

183 for _c in range(N_CF): 

184 w = b_prev + an / w 

185 an = an + (b_prev - x_f) 

186 b_prev = b_prev - 2.0 

187 q_cf = tl.exp(log_x_term - tl.log(w)) 

188 

189 # Path 3: DLMF 8.12.4 asymptotic expansion for large a with x ~ a: 

190 # Q(a,x) ~ 0.5 erfc(eta sqrt(a/2)) + e^{-a eta^2 / 2} 

191 # * sum_k c_k(eta) / a^k / sqrt(2 pi a), 

192 # with sigma = (x-a)/a, eta = sgn(x-a) sqrt(-2(log(1+sigma)-sigma)). 

193 # c_k(eta) = sum_n d[k,n] eta^n from DLMF table 8.12.1; for a > 10 and 

194 # fp32 output only c_0..c_3 are above the rounding floor, and each is 

195 # truncated at the term that falls below it (8/5/3/1 coefficients). 

196 # The literals are inlined because a `@triton.jit` body cannot read a 

197 # module-level table, and inlining also removes 64 scalar global loads 

198 # per element that the previous revision issued from `d_ptr`. 

199 sigma = (x_f - a_f) / a_f 

200 root = tl.sqrt(_eta_sq(sigma)) 

201 eta = tl.where(sigma > 0.0, root, tl.where(sigma < 0.0, -root, 0.0)) 

202 

203 c0 = -2.185448510679992e-06 

204 c0 = c0 * eta + 3.919263178522438e-05 

205 c0 = c0 * eta + (-0.0001787551440329218) 

206 c0 = c0 * eta + 0.0003527336860670194 

207 c0 = c0 * eta + 0.0011574074074074073 

208 c0 = c0 * eta + (-0.014814814814814815) 

209 c0 = c0 * eta + 0.08333333333333333 

210 c0 = c0 * eta + (-0.3333333333333333) 

211 

212 c1 = 0.00020576131687242798 

213 c1 = c1 * eta + (-0.0009902263374485596) 

214 c1 = c1 * eta + 0.0026455026455026454 

215 c1 = c1 * eta + (-0.003472222222222222) 

216 c1 = c1 * eta + (-0.001851851851851852) 

217 

218 c2 = 0.0007716049382716049 

219 c2 = c2 * eta + (-0.002681327160493827) 

220 c2 = c2 * eta + 0.004133597883597884 

221 

222 c3 = 0.0006494341563786008 

223 

224 a_inv = 1.0 / a_f 

225 poly_sum = c3 * a_inv + c2 

226 poly_sum = poly_sum * a_inv + c1 

227 poly_sum = poly_sum * a_inv + c0 

228 

229 q_asym = 0.5 * (1.0 - tl.math.erf(eta * tl.sqrt(a_f * 0.5))) 

230 q_asym = q_asym + tl.exp(-0.5 * a_f * eta * eta) * poly_sum / tl.sqrt( 

231 2.0 * 3.141592653589793 * a_f 

232 ) 

233 

234 # Per-element path selection. Note: a plain two-level 

235 # `tl.where(use_asym, q_asym, tl.where(use_series, q_series, q_cf))` 

236 # blows the XPU uni_sram pass (three distinct live values); the 

237 # mask-and-sum form is NaN-safe (unselected lanes are forced to 0.0 

238 # before summing) and compiles fine. Because exactly one term survives, 

239 # the [0, 1] projection is applied once to the sum rather than to each 

240 # branch. 

241 use_asym = (a_f > 10.0) & (tl.abs(sigma) < 0.4) 

242 use_series = (x_f < (a_f + 1.0)) & ~use_asym 

243 use_cf = ~use_asym & ~use_series 

244 computed = ( 

245 tl.where(use_asym, q_asym, 0.0) 

246 + tl.where(use_series, q_series, 0.0) 

247 + tl.where(use_cf, q_cf, 0.0) 

248 ) 

249 computed = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(computed, 0.0), 1.0) 

250 

251 # Boundary and infinity handling: 

252 # Q(a, 0) = 1, Q(inf, x) = 1, Q(a, inf) = 0, Q(inf, inf) = NaN, 

253 # out-of-domain (a <= 0 or x < 0) gives NaN. 

254 inf_result = tl.where( 

255 is_inf_x & is_inf_a, 

256 float("nan"), 

257 tl.where(is_inf_x, 0.0, tl.where(is_inf_a, 1.0, float("nan"))), 

258 ) 

259 result = tl.where( 

260 is_finite, 

261 tl.where(in_domain, computed, float("nan")), 

262 inf_result, 

263 ) 

264 

265 tl.store(out_ptr + offsets, result.to(out_ptr.type.element_ty), mask=mask) 

266

268def _launch(out: torch.Tensor, a: torch.Tensor, x: torch.Tensor): 

269 a_c = a.contiguous() 

270 x_c = x.contiguous() 

271 was_noncontig = not out.is_contiguous() 

272 out_c = out.contiguous() if was_noncontig else out 

273 

274 n = out_c.numel() 

275 if n > 0: 

276 BLOCK = 512 

277 grid = (triton.cdiv(n, BLOCK),) 

278 igammac_kernel_xpu[grid]( 

279 a_c, 

280 x_c, 

281 out_c, 

282 n, 

283 BLOCK_SIZE=BLOCK, 

284 N_SER=24, 

285 N_CF=18, 

286 buffer_size_limit=2048, 

287 ) 

288 

289 if was_noncontig: 

290 out.copy_(out_c) 

291 return out

294def igammac(a: torch.Tensor, x: torch.Tensor, *, out: torch.Tensor = None): 

295 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN IGAMMAC") 

296 if a.device.type != flag_gems.device: 

297 raise ValueError(f"igammac: first input tensor must be on {flag_gems.device}") 

298 if x.device.type != flag_gems.device: 

299 raise ValueError(f"igammac: second input tensor must be on {flag_gems.device}") 

300 

301 if not a.is_floating_point(): 

302 a = a.to(torch.get_default_dtype()) 

303 if not x.is_floating_point(): 

304 x = x.to(torch.get_default_dtype()) 

305 if a.dtype not in (torch.float32, torch.float64) or x.dtype not in ( 

306 torch.float32, 

307 torch.float64, 

308 ): 

309 raise RuntimeError( 

310 f"igammac Triton kernel supports fp32/fp64, but got " 

311 f"a.dtype={a.dtype}, x.dtype={x.dtype}" 

312 ) 

313 

314 if out is None: 

315 out_dtype = torch.promote_types(a.dtype, x.dtype) 

316 out = torch.empty_like(a, dtype=out_dtype, device=a.device) 

317 else: 

318 if out.device.type != flag_gems.device: 

319 raise ValueError( 

320 f"igammac_out: output tensor must be on {flag_gems.device}" 

321 ) 

322 if not out.is_floating_point(): 

323 raise TypeError("igammac_out: output tensor must be a floating point type") 

324 if a.numel() != x.numel() or a.numel() != out.numel(): 

325 raise ValueError( 

326 "igammac_out: input and output must have the same number of elements" 

327 ) 

328 

329 if a.dtype != out.dtype: 

330 a = a.to(out.dtype) 

331 if x.dtype != out.dtype: 

332 x = x.to(out.dtype) 

333 

334 _launch(out, a, x) 

335 return out 

336

338def igammac_out(a: torch.Tensor, x: torch.Tensor, out: torch.Tensor): 

339 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN IGAMMAC_OUT") 

340 return igammac(a, x, out=out)
